intelligence.description: Colossal Biosciences develops genetic engineering and computational-biology technology for conservation and de-extinction projects.
company: Colossal Biosciences was founded to develop technologies that can support de-extinction and conservation efforts. Its work spans computational biology, genome engineering, reproductive technology, and species-specific programs involving animals such as mammoths, thylacines, and dodos.

In January 2025, Colossal announced a $200 million Series C led by TWG Global at a $10.2 billion valuation. The investment case rests less on a single species project than on whether the underlying technology can produce durable applications in conservation, animal health, and biotechnology.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Colossal is an unusual private-market example of a platform-biotech valuation being driven by long-duration scientific optionality. It shows how capital is pricing genomic tools, high-profile research programs, and potential spinout businesses before conventional revenue scale is established.

changed.text: Colossal is founded to develop de-extinction and conservation technologies.
The company raises Series B financing to expand its genetic-engineering work.
A $200M Series C values Colossal at $10.2B.

takeaways: The valuation is tied to platform technology and long-term scientific optionality, not mature operating earnings.
Conservation and genetic-engineering applications could matter more commercially than any one de-extinction program.
Scientific, regulatory, and commercialization timelines are major risks.
The company must demonstrate that its underlying tools can create repeatable businesses beyond research milestones.
